quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 results (6-K): revenue of $569,925 from non-recurring engineering services and product sales, up 13% from the first quarter ($503,389) and 112% from $268,469 a year earlier, its sixth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth; research and development of $5.8 million versus $3.1 million a year earlier; quarter-end cash and short-term investments of $796.3 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue $569,925, up 13% QoQ and 112% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 6-K on customers: in May 2026 it entered a supply agreement establishing a strategic joint development and commercial technology partnership with Lumilens, under which Lumilens placed an initial purchase order for POET Optical Interposer-based engines valued at $50 million, the first phase of a supplier relationship that could scale to $500+ million in cumulative purchases over five years. Subsequent to quarter end POET received a new $2.4 million purchase order from an existing customer, completed an agreement with a Tier 1 laser company to develop an external light source engine, and entered an exclusive arrangement with a supplier for a component that enhances the output power of its Blazar hybrid laser.
quarterly_data.figure: Lumilens initial PO $50 million (could scale to $500+ million over five years); new $2.4 million PO

quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 financial-statement notes (deferred customer consideration): share purchase warrants were granted to a customer, not named in the note, in connection with a supply agreement in which the customer is expected to purchase up-to $500 million of products from the Company; 2,292,140 of the 22,921,408 warrants have vested and the remainder become exercisable as certain payment milestones are met.
quarterly_data.figure: customer expected to purchase up-to $500 million of products (unnamed customer)

quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 outlook (6-K): it expects to begin shipping substantial numbers of production units for qualification in the remaining quarters of 2026. CEO Suresh Venkatesan: the optical engine production ramp remains on schedule for the second half of 2026, and the new capital positions POET to accelerate expansion of manufacturing capacity in support of anticipated customer demand, including the production ramp associated with the Lumilens collaboration.
quarterly_data.figure: production units shipping for qualification in the remaining quarters of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 MD&A milestones and spending plan: 800G / 1.6T Tx prototypes in Q4 2026 and production in Q2 2027; light sources for AI prototype in Q4 2026 and production in Q2 2027; module development prototype in Q1 2027 and production in Q3 2027; Malaysia expansion of $7,000,000 over Q3 2025 - Q3 2026; $44,000,000 in total for R&D programs, Malaysia expansion and corporate development. It has an approved 2026 capital budget of $14,500,000 (with $5,508,836 spent on capital expenses in the first half) and intends to spend approximately $26,000,000 in 2026-2027 on modules and high-speed optical engines. Its production equipment has been transferred out of China to Globetronics and NationGate in Malaysia and the joint venture with Sanan IC has been dissolved.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T Tx production Q2 2027; light sources production Q2 2027; 2026 capital budget $14,500,000; ~$26,000,000 in 2026-2027

quarterly_data.signal: POET's Q2 2026 6-K on partners: on March 16, 2026 it announced a strategic collaboration with LITEON Technology to co-develop next-generation optical communication modules on POET's optical interposer platform, and on March 17, 2026 the joint development with Lessengers of a 1.6T 2xDR4 optical transceiver module for AI clusters. The notes record a $2,955,150 purchase of 4,500 redeemable convertible preferred shares (4.99%) of Lessengers Inc.. Its product list includes 400G/800G FR4 Tx and Rx, 1.6T 4xFR4 Rx, 200G/lane Tx and Rx for 1.6T and 3.2T chipsets and C-Band and O-Band LightBar external light sources.
